Computed for each district and each day; regencies and provinces take the highest status of their districts.

Landslides use H{17} (thresholds {18}/{19}/{20} mm), soil saturation (moisture {21}–{22} cm ≥ {23} and {24}-day rain ≥ {25} mm, or {26}-day rain ≥ {27} mm if moisture is missing), hourly rain, and InaRISK landslide hazard. kamus.Tab Insight menulis kesimpulan langsung: The Insight tab writes the conclusion directly in each chart's title, e.g. "hotspots rose in {0} of {1} provinces". The numbers in that title are computed automatically from the same data files as the other tabs; no number is typed by hand. The current day is excluded from comparisons because it is not yet complete.
kamus.Tab Keputusan membandingkan empat piliha: The Decisions tab compares four options for one season: A business as usual, B early warning + standby command posts, C plus pumps and drainage, D plus SAR and logistics readiness. Baseline impacts come from BNPB history (deaths, displaced people, damaged houses per year). Because many figures are still estimates, the calculation is repeated {0} times with the numbers randomised within their ranges. A measure is recommended if its net benefit is positive in at least {1} of the runs.
kamus.Tab Keputusan membandingkan empat strate: The Decisions tab compares four strategies for one season per province: A business as usual, B prevention and initial attack, C = B plus canal blocking, D = B plus helicopters and weather modification. For each strategy we compute how many hectares could be kept from burning, their value in rupiah (economic, health, and carbon losses), and the cost. Because many figures are still estimates, the calculation is repeated {0} times with numbers randomised within their ranges.
kamus.Tab Simulasi menjalankan aturan yang sam: The Simulation tab runs exactly the same rules as the daily status, but with altered inputs: rainfall multiplied by {0}, or {1} {2}-day rainfall forced to at least a set number of mm, soil assumed saturated, rivers assumed to reach the {3}- or {4}-year flood, or a high tide. Without a scenario, the result must match the map; the tab checks this itself and shows the result of the check.

kamus.Tiap kompleks diberi satu dari empat sta: Each fire complex is given one of four action statuses: routine prevention, joint patrol, initial attack standby, suppression priority. The status depends on two things: how large the fire seen by satellite is, and how dangerous the weather is. Weather can only raise the status, never lower it. Priority complexes are then ranked by score so crews know which to reach first.
kamus.Tiap kompleks siaga atau prioritas di {0: Each watch or priority fire complex in {0} provinces is assigned to the nearest permanent base (permanent command post or Daops headquarters) if ≤ {1} km. The rest are grouped by regency and given forward command posts using the same greedy maximal covering (radius {2} km, until all are covered), weight = ({3} if priority, {4} if watch) × max({5} px{6}). Candidate sites = villages within the complex box ± {7}°; if there is no village data, the district centroid; if still empty, the complex point itself. Currently {8} forward command posts.
kamus.Tiap kotak = berapa persen dari {0} sken: Each box = the percentage of the {0} ECMWF weather scenarios that produce that condition. {1} means {2} of {3} scenarios: a probability, not a certainty. Hover for the median FWI and its range.
kamus.Tiap malam pukul {0} WIB komputer menjal: Every night at {0} WIB the computer runs the same sequence of programs: fetching the latest satellite and weather data, recalculating all figures, then testing them. If a test fails, that day's data is not published and the page keeps the previous data. {1} was chosen because data from the daytime satellite pass (± {2} local time) only reaches NASA about {3} hours later.
kamus.Tiap pagi pukul {0} WIB komputer menjala: Every morning at {0} WIB the computer runs the same sequence of programs: it fetches the latest rainfall forecast, river discharge, sea tide, and BMKG warnings, recalculates the status of every district, then publishes it. Before starting, the calculation rules are tested; if a test fails, nothing is published and the page keeps yesterday's data. The {1} start was chosen because the weather model run at {2} WIB ({3} UTC) has reached the data providers by then.
